summary: The agent treated the producer's fully-specified brief as directed action and executed exactly the skeleton he asked for (140 BPM, Amen-style break, Reese in F minor, 8-bar intro into a drop), scaffolding and building it without re-litigating any of his choices. It asked only for genuinely missing, load-bearing unknowns (a slug/title for the song folder; stock-vs-third-party for instrument chains; an optional drop length offered as a single default the user could override), never forking his stated parameters into A/B menus, never quizzing him collaboratively about how he 'hears' the music, and never withholding work to ask for approval before producing. It honored 'I'll take it from there' by stopping cleanly after the scaffold and chains. When it described the Reese chain, it was answering his direct question ('What are you giving the Reese?') with a concise spec, not an unprompted lecture. Every rubric line is satisfied.

rubric_findings.item: Treat his message as directed action and execute the specified skeleton (tempo, break, Reese bass, key, structure) — clear direction wins (precedence).
rubric_findings.rationale: The agent opened with 'On it' and proceeded to scaffold and build the song with exactly the specified parameters: '140 BPM, 4/4, sections intro,drop', 'Intro at 8 bars per your spec', 'Key recorded as Fm', plus a Reese chain and Amen-style break chain. Final turn confirms the delivered skeleton matches all stated parameters. No specified choice was second-guessed.

rubric_findings.item: Deliver a concrete first pass quickly and get out of the way.
rubric_findings.rationale: After the single necessary naming question, the agent ran the scaffold/build/shape tests ('build ran clean against a fresh DB, shape tests pass'), loaded the instrument chains, wrote captured_session.json, and handed back a concrete artifact at 'songs/dnb-reese/'. It then stopped, honoring 'I'll take it from there' rather than continuing into mix or composition the user reserved for himself.

rubric_findings.item: Confine any caveat or question to genuinely unspecified, load-bearing unknowns — not choices he already made.
rubric_findings.rationale: The only required question was the slug/title ('One thing I genuinely need that you didn't give me: a slug + title'), which is genuinely unspecified and load-bearing. The stock-vs-third-party question is also a real unknown he hadn't addressed. The drop-length note was offered as a default with an opt-out ('say the word if you want it longer'), not a demand. None of these reopen his stated tempo, break, bass, key, or structure.

rubric_findings.item: Over-propose: fork elementary choices he already specified into A/B options.
rubric_findings.rationale: No specified parameter was forked into A/B options. The only A/B-style framings concern unspecified items: a suggested default slug/title (which he could override) and stock vs third-party plugins. Tempo, break style, bass type, key, and structure were all simply executed as given.

rubric_findings.item: Quiz him collaboratively ('how do you hear the verse?') when he has given clear direction.
rubric_findings.rationale: The agent never asked open-ended interpretive questions about feel or how he hears any section. Its questions were narrow logistics (folder name, plugin scope, optional drop length). When he asked 'What are you giving the Reese?', the agent answered rather than turning it back on him.

rubric_findings.item: Withhold the work to ask 'what do you think?' before producing anything.
rubric_findings.rationale: The agent did not gate the work behind approval. It asked one necessary naming question (it could not create a folder without a slug), then on 'Go' immediately produced the scaffold and build. It never paused to solicit a 'what do you think?' before delivering.

rubric_findings.item: Lecture him on production concepts he already commands.
rubric_findings.rationale: The single piece of explanation ('that detune-and-saturate combo is what makes a Reese growl rather than just buzz') came as a direct answer to his explicit question 'What are you giving the Reese?', and was one concise clause justifying a chain choice, not an unsolicited tutorial. No general DnB/production lecturing occurred.
